description: Open-air Hindu street shrine of the Erawan type -- a gilded four-faced deity image under a small open pavilion on a raised platform, ringed with garlands and offered elephant figures.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small open-air shrine pavilion on a raised square granite platform, four slender gilded columns carrying a tiered pointed gilded canopy roof with no walls, a gilded four-faced seated deity figure on a stone pedestal at the centre, rows of small carved wooden elephant figures massed on the platform edge, low gilded railing with brass candle and incense trays around the outside. No flowers, no garlands, no plants, no fabric, no people -- only stone, gilt, brass and carved wood. Materials: Bright gold leaf on the figure, columns and canopy, dark oiled teak elephants, thick candle wax runs and ash on the brass trays, polished dark granite platform and pedestal.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91 on the regenerated plate (no organics). Silhouette 0.93 against the Meshy proxy (mean 0.036/0.035 of height, the one flagged band the solid rail panel against an open lattice); structure 0.91 with four components and three instanced sets; form 0.88, held back by a 1.3 m figure that carries pose and proportion but no face or robe; material 0.89 with three canvases. 13,920/16,000 triangles, 7/12 draw calls, 5/12 materials, 7/12 unique geometries, ~65 ms factory.

featureReviews.evidence: A 1.3 m seated gilded figure on the pedestal's gilt cushion: crossed legs with knee spheres, a torso tube from hips to a neck with shoulders wider than the waist, a head with four brow lobes and a tiered hair spire, the right forearm raised with an open hand, the left arm down to the knee holding a trident. Visible through the colonnade from az 60-120; the hero 45 frame puts the front column across it.
featureReviews.notes: The first emit read the station tube's format wrong ([x, y, z, r, r] where tubeAlong takes [z, cx, cy, rx, ry] along z) and put the torso outside the base as a flat capsule while a bell of head and spire sat on the pedestal; the torso is built upright then stood up with rotateX(-pi/2). A torso wider at the hips than the shoulders still read as a bell, so the stations were re-cut with the shoulders as the widest ring and the legs ellipsoid narrowed from 0.88 to 0.72 m. Robe, face and hands are not authored at 1.3 m.

featureReviews.evidence: Four gilded columns at +-1.30 with ringed shafts, square bases and bracket capitals under an eaves beam; a steep concave-pyramid canopy 3.56 m square at the eaves (4.35) rising to 5.70 with 0.28 m upturned corners, a fascia, corner balls and a ball finial to 6.00; nothing between the columns.
featureReviews.notes: The preamble's hipRoof samples eight points per ring and creased the faces, so the roof is a bespoke square pyramid sampled eight times per side over twelve rings. Its winding was wrong twice -- the fascia black, then the slopes black -- and settled by probing the built bundle's face normals under Node (slopes had face normals pointing DOWN) rather than by eye. Band table against the Meshy proxy: eaves 3.6 m (band 7), 1.5 m at 4.8-5.4 (band 8, +0.05 residual from the lifted corners), columns 2.7 m apart (bands 4-6 within 0.025).

featureReviews.evidence: Eight carved teak elephants 0.56 m long -- body, head, trunk tube, ears, tusks, four legs, tail -- two per side on the platform floor walking anticlockwise, and eight brass trays on the lower step. No garlands, flowers or fabric anywhere.
featureReviews.notes: The first pass at 0.44 m in a dark #5A3220 read as brown crabs; enlarged to 0.56 x 0.40 m and lifted to #74401F (saturation 0.73, so the tone holds on chroma against the backdrop). The trunk tube had the same station-format bug as the deity and now runs forward and down. Eight instances of ~900 triangles are two thirds of the prop's triangle count and are what distinguishes this shrine from a plain pavilion, as the registry notes require.

featureReviews.evidence: Five materials: veined granite (vein-toned material under a marble multiplier tile), gold leaf at #DCB04A with metalness 0.35, oiled teak, brass, and a white carrier for the rail's painted key-fret. Three post-construction canvases at 4 MB.
featureReviews.notes: The granite field ships near luma 95 against a measured 62 because a low-chroma grey at 62 sits on the backdrop's 58 and reads as holes on the back-lit frame; the veins carry the identity. The gilt's metalness is held to 0.35: a metal with no environment map has its diffuse scaled by (1 - metalness) and the first render's gold was brown at 0.55. The rail lattice is a painted canvas because a multiplier can only darken -- gold over grey cannot be painted onto either existing material, hence the fifth.

name: Brahman Street Shrine
nameTh: ศาลพระพรหม
notes: An open-air shrine, so it has no walls at all -- four columns, a canopy roof and an open platform. That openness is the point and must not be closed in, because the deity figure has to be visible from the street on every side. The massed small elephant figures and the looped garlands are accumulated offerings and are what distinguishes this from a plain pavilion, so they are part of the asset rather than separate dressing. This is a Hindu Brahman shrine and its four-faced seated figure is deliberately not a Buddha image. Declared at 6 m, just below the building-part category's 8 m prior. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.
